title: Condorcet consistency forces dictatorship
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f$ assign an outcome in $\{-1,1\}$ to each profile of $n$ voters’ rankings of three candidates. Suppose $f$ is unanimous, meaning it selects $1$ on the profile where every voter ranks each pair in favor of $1$, and selects $-1$ on the profile where every voter ranks each pair in favor of $-1$. Suppose also that for every ranking profile, the three pairwise outcomes have a Condorcet winner. Then there is a voter $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ such that $f$ returns that voter’s pairwise preferences on every profile.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps three-candidate ranking profiles of $n$ voters to pairwise sign outcomes
Every ranking profile has a societal Condorcet winner
